review_notes:
I read the whole file. It has one helper namespace (`FinSepAux`) and one long theorem, `solution`. The helper namespace has these declarations:
- `F`, a def built with `comap`.
- `mem_F`, proved by `Iff.rfl`.
- `ιF`.
- `eF`.
- `coe_eF`, proved by `rfl`.
- `eq_top_of_generators_mem`.

None of these has a `@[simp]` attribute, and none defines a rewrite rule that could loop or compete with another.

The only candidate was a missing simp tag on `mem_F` and `coe_eF`. A search of the repo found these names used in 13 files, but the `FinSepAux` hits look like local copies of the same helper namespace. In this file, `mem_F` is used once, as `exact mem_F z`, after an explicit `rw [IntermediateField.mem_extendScalars]`. `coe_eF` is not used in the proof of `solution`. The `simp` calls in `solution` are `simp [Polynomial.eval₂_sub, sub_eq_zero]` and `simp [sub_eq_zero]`. Neither needs `mem_F` or `coe_eF`, so tagging them would not improve any use I could see. Adding global simp lemmas about a local def, only because the statements are `rfl`, is the kind of change the rubric warns against.

The long `attribute [-simp]` and `attribute [-instance]` header lines only remove simp lemmas and instances from other files for this file's elaboration. I did not treat that as a defect in this file's own simp interface. I did not look at those removed lemmas, so I may have missed a simp-set problem there. I did not run Lean.
